description: OS Net is the Ordnance Survey network of about 120 Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) base stations across Great Britain, delivering real-time and post-processed correction data for centimetre-level positioning in surveying, mapping, construction, agriculture and autonomous systems. Recorded OS Net data is published in the standard RINEX version 3 format as hourly files at a 30-second rate, and it is free to download through the OS Data Hub after registering for the free OS OpenData Plan; the data is also available through an API, and real-time correction services are sold through commercial partners. The page says the network supports the National Geographic Database, HM Land Registry and Met Office forecasting. No licence is stated on the page beyond the OS OpenData Plan terms. Caveats: the free product is recorded data for post-processing, not the real-time correction stream, and coverage is Great Britain only. It supports positioning infrastructure and GNSS resilience studies, for example ionospheric effects of space weather on positioning; there are no related records in the catalogue yet on this branch.
